title: Data Sovereignty Routing Mosaic: tenant-scoped EU residency + tier fallback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers with EU-only data residency and regulatory constraints require every inference request to stay within EU jurisdictions and forbid cross-border model execution. Current routing can accidentally route to non-EU capacity during degraded states or bursting, and some tenant-level allow/deny controls are not expressive enough for mixed-tier fallbacks.

Goal: Implement a 'Routing Mosaic' policy layer that deterministically enforces tenant-scoped residency constraints while supporting tier-aware fallbacks to compatible model variants (EU-hosted, quantized/local replicas) without violating egress constraints. Provide a clear config schema, runtime enforcement hooks, observability, and a safe rollout path.

Scope: design and implement the policy evaluator and runtime gating (policy + enforcement) for Redwood's request router. This includes: 1) tenant-level residency policy evaluation, 2) per-tenant allowlist/denylist for regions and edge-fallbacks, 3) tier routing rules (hosted/dedicated/private) with precedence, 4) automatic variant mapping to EU-compatible model alternatives when primary is not available, and 5) audit logging and alerts for policy violations.

Out of scope: billing model changes, long-term UI for editing granular policies (console tweaks will be follow-up PM work).
acceptance_criteria: Routing Mosaic policy accepts tenant config and computes a deterministic routing decision that never routes EU-residency traffic outside EU zones.

When primary capacity is unavailable, router selects a model variant that is EU-hosted or runs in-customer VPC; if none exist, request is rejected with specific HTTP 451-like error and audit log entry.
Config supports tenant allowlists and denylists for regions and tiers with clear precedence rules; tests validate precedence matrix.
End-to-end integration tests covering normal, degraded, and burst scenarios; no cross-region egress observed in test harness.
Observability: per-tenant routing decisions logged, metric exposed for 'policy-enforced-fallback' and dashboard created in console-2025.02 release.
Performance: policy evaluation adds <1ms median latency at router injection point under 95th percentile load (validated in benchmark harness).
design_notes: Policy model: decorators combined into a small expression language: residency == EU AND tenant.blocked_regions NOT CONTAINS eu-west-1 => allow EU-only routing; default deny-exit.
Precedence: tenant-level denylist > tenant-level allowlist > default org policy > global emergency-exit flag.
Fallback mapping: primary model -> candidate variants list ordered by (region affinity, model-compatibility, cost-tier). The runtime will only pick variants that satisfy 'residency' predicate.
Enforcement points: router decision service (fast path), and enforcement middleware at gateway to reject any accidental non-compliant handoffs between internal services.

Audit: immutable audit record with decision reason, policy version, selected variant id (or rejection code), and trace id. Records stored in append-only EU region bucket for customers with residency=EU.
Config schema chosen to be human-editable YAML via console later; for now accept JSON via control-plane API and via tenant bootstrap files for Private deployments.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the policy evaluator behind 'routing_mosaic' gate (control-plane flag).
2) Deploy policy evaluator to staging and run synthetic traffic harness with residency-indexed probes across burst scenarios.
3) Onboard 1 internal tenant (non-customer) with EU_ONLY to validate logs and dashboards (2-week canary).
4) Gradually enable for small customers that opt-in with rollback window; monitor 'policy-violation' metrics and latency regressions.
5) After 4 weeks of stability, flip global default to enforce for all tenants that declare residency=EU_ONLY and document migration steps for Dedicated and Private customers.
tests: Unit: policy expression evaluator matrix tests for residency/allow/deny/tier precedence (coverage >= 95%).

Integration: router + serving runtime harness where we simulate primary capacity OOS and ensure fallback to EU variant occurs or request is denied with 451-like error with decision code 'RESIDENCY_NOCOMPAT'.
Load: policy evaluator stress test at QPS similar to router peak with latency SLAs measured (95th percentile < 3ms per evaluation).
Audit replay: ability to replay audit logs to assert no cross-region egress in test traces.
risks: If fallback variants are not pre-provisioned in EU, requests will be rejected causing customer-facing errors. Mitigation: preflight validator to ensure tenant has at least one compatible EU variant before enabling policy.
Performance overhead if policy evaluator becomes a blocking call on the hot path. Mitigation: cache decisions by (tenant, route, model, token_prefix_hash) and ensure TTLs are conservative.
Operational complexity for Dedicated/Private customers with mixed-region resources. Mitigation: provide validators and a mapping CLI to register local variants.
monitoring_and_dashboards: Metric: redwood.routing.policy.violation_count (alerts if > 0 for a tenant with residency=EU_ONLY)
Dashboard: per-tenant routing decisions, recent audit events table, 95th latency of policy eval, and fallback selection histogram.
Alert: pager if any tenant with residency=EU_ONLY observes >5 policy_rejections in 5m window or any 'egress_detected' audit flag.
